title: OTLP backpressure & storage tiering TF playbook (draft)
body:
Status: draft / sketch. Purpose: capture a pragmatic playbook + Terraform module notes for handling OTLP collector backpressure, local disk buffering, and long-term storage tiering in private deployments (VPC + on-prem). This is intended for infra engineers preparing upgrades or new customers with high-ingest workloads (high logs + traces + metrics).

Key goals:
- Avoid dropped telemetry during spikes while protecting collector memory/CPU.
- Provide TF module knobs for: persistent buffering (disk), bounded local retention, S3/remote archival, and backoff/failover to Kafka/Kinesis when remote is unavailable.
- Provide clear upgrade/canary plan for migrating existing deployments to OTEL Collector 0.xx (or internal fork) with minimal data loss.
- Offer observability guidance (Prometheus/Grafana dashboards & alerts) to detect buffer saturation, retries, and increased CPU.

Scope / Assumptions:
- Target customers: Redwood Private (VPC) and on-prem packaged deployments.
- We assume customers run the collector as a DaemonSet or dedicated StatefulSet depending on topology. TF modules must support both (helm_release + k8s_statefulset).
- Storage backends: local PVC (hostPath on air-gapped), S3-compatible (minio) for archival. Also support Kafka as durable sink for logs if direct OTLP endpoint is overloaded.

High-level strategy (short):
1) Configure Collector with bounded file-based queue (file_queue) + disk-based buffer + memory limits. Use file_queue for traces/logs, memory_queue for high-throughput short-lived metrics where feasible.
2) Expose relevant metrics (otelcol_queue_capacity, otelcol_queue_size_bytes, otelcol_exporter_retries, exporter_send_latency_ms) to Prometheus.
3) Add Prometheus rules & Grafana panels for buffer high-water (75%), near-full (90%), and saturation (95%). Add automated runbooks/alerts for saturation.
4) Terraform modules provide variables for: pvc_size_gb, queue_max_bytes, queue_max_items, buffer_cleanup_hours, archival_bucket, kafka_topic, kafka_retention_days, collector_version.

Suggested TF module surface (notes for implementer):
- Module name: telemetry/collector-buffering (path: modules/telemetry/collector-buffering)
- Inputs (string/number/bool):
  - collector_helm_chart (string)
  - collector_version (string)
  - enable_stateful (bool) -> create StatefulSet + PVC if true, else DaemonSet
  - pvc_size_gb (number)
  - pvc_storage_class (string)
  - use_file_queue (bool)
  - queue_max_bytes (number)
  - queue_max_items (number)
  - buffer_rotate_period_hours (number)
  - archival_enabled (bool)
  - archival_bucket (string)
  - archival_prefix (string)
  - kafka_enabled (bool)
  - kafka_brokers (list)
  - kafka_topic_logs (string)
  - kafka_retention_days (number)
  - prometheus_service_monitor_enabled (bool)
- Outputs: collector_service_name, pvc_claim_name, prometheus_service_monitor_name

TF implementation tips / pitfalls:
- PVC sizing: default 50GB for medium clusters (estimate: 1GB per 15k log events/day * retention window). Document that this is very workload-specific. Offer sample sizing table.
- When using hostPath on air-gapped: prefer a mount under /var/lib/redwood/otel-buffer and require an init container that sets permissions. Note security implications.
- Don't rely solely on otlp exporter retries for backpressure — retries increase memory usage. Prefer file_queue + bounded memory limits + exporter backoff.
- Ensure collector pod has podDisruptionBudget when using StatefulSet with PVC.

OTEL Collector config sketch (important knobs) — comments for ops:
- receivers: otlp
- processors:
  - memory_limiter:
      limit_mib: 2048
      spike_limit_mib: 256
      check_interval: 5s
  - queued_retry:
      enabled: true
      num_consumers: 2
      queue_size: "${var.queue_max_items}"   # for items-based queues
  - batch:
      send_batch_max_size: 8192
      timeout: 5s
- exporters:
  - otlp/http (primary)
  - kafka (logs fallback) configured with async produce and retries limited
- extensions: health_check, pprof, zpages (optional)

File-based queue example (collector distribution):
- Use `file_storage` / `storage` extension (if using contrib builds) with `dir:` pointing to mounted PVC. Configure `max_storage_size` == `pvc_size_gb`.
- When disk usage reaches high-watermark: exporter starts returning resource-exhausted which should be surfaced as metrics. Plan: automated alert and rate-limiter at ingress to protect collector.

Prometheus & Grafana: metrics & alerting checklist (panel / rule names):
- telemetry/collector_queue_fill_ratio (gauge) -> calc queue_size_bytes / queue_max_bytes
- telemetry/disk_buffer_usage_bytes
- telemetry/exporter_retry_count_total (delta)
- telemetry/memory_limiter_oom_events_total
- telemetry/queued_retry_sent_bytes
Alerts (severity mapping):
- P0: queue_fill_ratio > 0.98 for 2min -> page SRE + infra oncall
- P1: queue_fill_ratio > 0.9 for 10min -> slack #infra-telemetry
- P1: exporter_retry_rate > 50% for 5min -> investigate backend connectivity
- P2: disk_usage > 0.8 for 30min -> ops to consider increasing PVC or enabling archival

Log shipping fallback pattern (when upstream OTLP sinks full):
- Configure fluent-bit as local aggregator -> forward to Kafka topic logs-ingest.
- Consumer service reads Kafka and forwards to Redwood ingestion endpoints at controlled rate with backoff.
- Benefits: Kafka provides durable buffer across redeploys/collector restarts. Drawback: additional operational surface and eventual consistency.

Upgrade plan (for moving from current collector X -> target Y in private deployments):
Preparation (pre-upgrade):
- Create canary namespace + install new collector with same configuration except reduced ingestion rate (sample 5–10% of traffic).
- Add exporters to both old and new collectors pointing to a temporary compare endpoint (if possible) to sample outputs for QA.
- Run integration smoke-tests: ingest synthetic traces/logs/metrics at target TPS and confirm end-to-end.

Canary rollout:
- Start with 1 node/statefulset replica processing mirrored traffic for 48 hours.
- Monitor queue_fill_ratio, exporter_retries, CPU, memory, and disk. Compare to baseline.
- If metrics stable, increase mirrored traffic to 25% for 24 hours.
- After 72 total hours with no regression, schedule gradual rollout (10% nodes -> 50% -> 100%).

Rollback procedure:
- If any P0 alerts triggered, immediately switch traffic back to old collector (ingress routing) and scale down new collector.
- Preserve PVCs for postmortem. If new collector caused disk corruption, restore from snapshot.

Smoke-test commands (examples):
- telemetry/loader: quick load with otelcol-bench or rubeus-otel (whatever we standardize on). Example: `otel-bench --otlp-endpoint https://canary.collector.local:4317 --rate 2000/s --duration 10m`
- verify metrics: `kubectl port-forward svc/prometheus 9090:9090` then query `sum(rate(telemetry_collector_exporter_sent_total[1m]))`

Rollback notes & data retention during rollback:
- Important: when rolling back, do not immediately prune PVCs. Keep them for at least 72 hours to allow re-ingestion if needed. We should add a script in TF module for snapshotting PVC contents (for cloud PVs use snapshot class, for hostPath use tarball).

Open questions / TODOs (triage in next infra sync):
- Should we standardize on Kafka-based fallback for all on-prem customers or make it opt-in? (Cost + ops tradeoffs)
- How do we handle multi-tenant disk usage isolation on nodes where multiple tenants' buffers might contend? (cgroups? per-tenant quotas?)
- Container user permissions for hostPath mounts in air-gapped installs (work with security).
- Add CI job that runs a lightweight ingestion test against a dev cluster after every TF change to the module.

Runbook snippets (for paging):
1) Alert: collector_queue_fill_ratio > 0.98
   - First action: check Prometheus graph for the last 30m. `kubectl -n telemetry get pods -l app=otel-collector -o wide`
   - If pods show high CPU/memory: scale collector statefulset replica count (if using dedicated), or restart collector daemon on node with highest CPU after draining a node.
   - If disk at >95%: do quick archival -> run `kubectl exec -n telemetry $(pod) -- /opt/collector/bin/rotate-archive.sh` (script to upload oldest buffer files to archival_bucket).
2) Alert: exporter_retry_rate high and no connectivity issues in k8s network
   - Check remote endpoint (prod ingestion) health and rate-limiting (contact GTM if customer managed).
   - If remote is rate-limiting: flip to Kafka fallback (TF var kafka_enabled=true) and redeploy new collector config that sends to kafka.

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally prescriptive but lightweight. When we convert to a final playbook, split into two deliverables: 1) TF module (plumbing + defaults), 2) Runbook (alerts + escalation + commands + scripts).

References / links to internal artifacts: JIRA-OBS-5892 (buffering design epic), GH PR #210 contains initial TF module stub, Confluence page for architecture. Also see customer incident notes in JIRA-INC-4410 for example of disk buffer exhaustion event.

Authors / contact: Aisha Patel (owner), reach in Slack #infra-telemetry or ping Marco / Priya.

Last checklist before merging TF change to main (short):
- [ ] Module unit tests?
- [ ] Terraform plan reviewed by 2 infra engineers
- [ ] Helm values validated in dev cluster
- [ ] Canary deployment smoke tests added to CI

End of draft.
